rater_moves.moves: This is the mechanically generated `_assoc` variant: take the base naturality square for the associator tensored with an identity, whisker it on the right by an arbitrary further morphism, and reassociate the composites. No new mathematics beyond the base lemma.

This is the reassociated variant of the associator naturality lemma: take the base identity, post-compose (whisker) it with an arbitrary further morphism, and reassociate the composite using associativity of composition.

This is the reassociated form of the naturality square for the associator against an identity tensor: take the base naturality identity and post-compose both sides with an arbitrary morphism, reassociating the composites.
Unfold the evaluation semantics of the `succ` code: it takes the head of the input list and adds one, returning a singleton partial value; simp reduces both sides to the same term.
Unfold the evaluation of the succ code on an input list: it takes the head (with default 0) and adds one, so the result is Part.some [n+1]; closed by definitional simplification.
Unfold the evaluation of the successor code: it reads the head of the input list and returns the singleton list containing head+1, wrapped in Part.some; the whole thing computes definitionally.
Case analysis on the (impossible) derivation of n+1 <= 0: no constructor of Nat.le can produce it, so the goal is vacuously False. Nothing here is a citable lemma.
Introduce the hypothesis n+1 <= 0 and case on the inductive definition of Nat's order: neither constructor can produce a successor below zero, so the case analysis is vacuous and yields False.
Introduce the hypothesis n+1 <= 0 and observe no constructor of Nat.le can produce it; the whole proof is the vacuous case analysis, packaged in a generated match.
Unfold deleteVerts as the subgraph induced on the set difference, apply induce_adj, and rewrite membership in a set difference as membership plus non-membership.

Unfold deleteVerts as the induced subgraph on the vertex set minus the deleted set, apply the adjacency characterisation of induce, and expand set-difference membership into a conjunction with a negation.
Unfold deleteVerts as the induced subgraph on verts minus s, apply the adjacency description of induce, and simplify the resulting set-difference memberships into the conjunctive form.

Mechanically generated `_assoc` variant of coassociativity for a comonad in a bicategory: whisker the comul_assoc equation on the right by an arbitrary further 2-cell and reassociate the composites. The content is entirely the base lemma.

Reassociated form of the comonad coassociativity law in a bicategory: take comul_assoc and whisker it with an arbitrary further 2-morphism, reassociating the composite with associativity of composition.
Reassociated form of the comonad coassociativity law in a bicategory: take the comul_assoc 2-cell identity and post-compose it with an arbitrary 2-morphism, then reassociate the resulting composites.

Unfold IsLoopAt and IsNonloopAt to their incidence definitions and then push negations through the conjunction/double negation classically until the two sides of the iff coincide; the content is definitional unfolding plus propositional rearrangement.

Unfold IsLoopAt, Inc and IsNonloopAt to their underlying incidence statements, then the equivalence is pure propositional manipulation: push the negation through the conjunction/existential and cancel a double negation.

Unfold IsLoopAt and IsNonloopAt into their incidence conditions, then rearrange the resulting propositional formula by pushing the negation through the conjunction and eliminating a double negation classically.

Pure definitional monotonicity: a vertex cover condition says every edge meets the set, so enlarging the set along s <= t preserves it; the real work is a one-line membership chase hidden in an auto-generated private obligation.

Pure definitional monotonicity: a vertex cover meets every edge, so any superset of it does too; the real argument is unfolding IsVertexCover and chasing the subset hypothesis, and here it is buried in an auto-generated private lemma.

Unfold the vertex-cover condition and, for each edge, take the endpoint covered by the smaller set and push it into the larger set along the subset hypothesis. The real content is transitivity of membership through an inclusion.
An additive equivalence is in particular an additive-monoid-hom-class map, so the generic lemma that such maps preserve subtraction applies verbatim.
An additive equivalence is in particular a homomorphism of subtraction monoids, so the generic map_sub lemma applies directly; the proof is a one-line specialization.
An additive equivalence is an additive group hom, so subtraction is preserved by the general map_sub lemma for hom classes.
Machine-generated reassociated form of comp2_iso_inv in the pith of a bicategory: right-whisker the base equation and reassociate. The only mathematical input is the base lemma.
Same auto-generated reassociation pattern: take comp₂_iso_inv, whisker it with an arbitrary following morphism and reassociate. The mathematical content lives entirely in the base lemma.

Another reassoc-generated variant: whisker the base equation about the inverse of the composed 2-isomorphism in the Pith by a further morphism and reassociate. The mathematical content is entirely in the base lemma.

Given two valuation bounds with one below the other, show the induced additive subgroup of elements with small value is contained in the larger one; the whole content is chaining an element's value bound through transitivity of the order on the value group.

Given gamma <= gamma', show the subgroup {x | v x <= gamma} is contained in {x | v x <= gamma'}: take a member, its valuation is <= gamma <= gamma', so transitivity of <= in the value group closes it.
Given gamma1 <= gamma2, an element with v x <= gamma1 also satisfies v x <= gamma2; the whole argument is transitivity of the order on the value group, so the subgroup inclusion follows pointwise.
Rewrite the bitvector of the USize coercion using the existing toBitVec_toUSize lemma, then push the resulting width cast through setWidth by congruence and close by reflexivity.

Rewrite the 64-bit bitvector of the USize conversion using the known toBitVec-of-toUSize lemma, then push that rewrite under the width cast by congruence and close by reflexivity; the real content is width bookkeeping between numBits and 64 via setWidth.
Unfold toUSize/toBitVec64 and rewrite with the known description of (x.toUSize).toBitVec, then push the rewrite under the BitVec width cast by congruence and close by reflexivity.

An auto-generated obligation for transporting a colimit along an isomorphism of cocones: rewrite the composite with the iso inverse using the cancellation lemma and close by uniqueness of the descent morphism; most of the term is rewrite/congruence residue.

Auto-generated obligation for transporting a colimit along an isomorphism of cocones: the descent morphism through the iso is unique, so rewrite the composite with the iso inverse using the cancellation law and apply uniqueness of cocone morphisms. Much of the term is rewriting scaffolding.

An auto-generated side obligation for transporting a colimit along an isomorphism of cocones: rewrite the composite with the iso's inverse using comp_inv_eq, then close with uniqueness of the morphism out of the colimit. Most of the term is rewriting scaffolding produced by the tactic block.

This is the machine-generated reassociated form of lift_snd_comp_fst_comp: whisker the base equation on the right and reassociate composition. No new mathematics beyond associativity plus the base lemma.

Mechanically derived reassociated form of an existing lemma: whisker the base equation lift_snd_comp_fst_comp on the right by an arbitrary morphism and reassociate. No new mathematics beyond the base lemma and associativity.

A reassoc-generated variant: take the base identity about lift, snd, fst and the braiding, post-compose both sides with an arbitrary further morphism, and reassociate. No new mathematics beyond the base lemma plus associativity of composition.
Unfold the Int8 order relations to the corresponding order on the underlying integers via toInt, then apply transitivity of < with <= on Int.
Unfold the Int8 order relations to the corresponding order on the underlying integers via toInt, then apply the integer mixed-transitivity lemma.
Rewrite both Int8 order relations into their defining statements about toInt, then apply transitivity of < with <= on the integers.

Chain two known bridges: the implementation's minEntry? agrees with the model version minEntry?ₘ, which in turn agrees with the list-level minEntry? on the tree's list model, using the ordering invariant.

Chain the implementation's minEntry? through the intermediate model function minEntry?ₘ: one lemma takes minEntry? to minEntry?ₘ, a second takes minEntry?ₘ to the list-model minEntry?, and the two are composed by rewriting.
Chain the two bridging lemmas through the intermediate model function minEntry?-sub-m: the implementation agrees with it, and it agrees with the list-model minimum on toListModel.

Translate each congruence into a divisibility of the difference, then use that the lcm divides a number exactly when both do; here the translation is carried out by simp with generated private lemmas.

Turn both congruences into divisibility statements about a - b and use that m and n both divide a difference exactly when their lcm does; here that reduction is packaged as a simp certificate closing the iff to True.
Translate each congruence into divisibility of the difference, then use that a number is divisible by both moduli exactly when it is divisible by their least common multiple.
Move both sides to the underlying bitvector via toBitVec_not and injectivity of toBitVec, then the statement is the bitvector-level commutation of complement across an equation.

Transport both sides to bitvectors via toBitVec, use that complement commutes with the representation map, and finish with the corresponding bitvector commutation of negation; the surrounding structure is a simp certificate.
Transfer the statement along toBitVec, rewriting complement of a UInt8 into complement of its BitVec, then use the BitVec-level commutation of not across an equation; simp closes the resulting iff.
Case analysis on the walk: non-nilness rules out the empty walk, so the walk ends in a cons and the required adjacency is exactly the edge stored there.

Case on the walk (it is not nil, so it ends in a cons/concat step) and read off the adjacency of the penultimate vertex with the endpoint from the final edge of the walk; the argument is an induction packaged into a generated helper.
Case on the walk being non-nil (so it has a penultimate vertex) and read off adjacency from the final edge of the walk; the case analysis lives in a generated proof helper.

Prove both directions of the iff: unfold semicontinuity as a neighbourhood condition on sublevel/superlevel sets, and convert between 'is a neighbourhood of each of its points' and openness using IsOpen.mem_nhds.

Prove both implications of the iff: unfold semicontinuity as a neighborhood-filter condition and, in one direction, use that an open set containing the point is a neighborhood; the other direction is the definitional membership rewriting of the sublevel/superlevel set.

Split the iff; the forward direction turns openness of a sublevel/superlevel set into a neighborhood statement via IsOpen.mem_nhds, the reverse rewrites the nhds condition back to openness, with simp normalizing the set-builder form.

This is the order dual of the already-proved statement about eventual upper bounds: transport to the order-dual type, where the linear order and topology are the dual instances, and apply the dual lemma.
Order duality: the statement about eventually-const-le is exactly the already-proved eventually-le-const statement read in the order dual, with the dual order and topology instances transported.
Pure dualization: pass to the order dual, where the statement becomes the already-proved 'eventually <= const iff for all greater, eventually < const', and transport back.

Given the edge from the start to v and v on the path's support, compare the single-edge path u→v with the truncation of p up to v; in an acyclic graph paths between two vertices are unique (Subsingleton), so the two agree and v must be p.snd.

In an acyclic graph paths between two vertices are unique, so the single-edge path from the start along the given adjacency and the path obtained by truncating the given walk up to that vertex must coincide (Subsingleton.elim), which forces the claimed identification of the second vertex.

Take the initial segment of the walk up to the given vertex, which is again a path, and compare it with the single-edge path given by the adjacency; in an acyclic graph paths between two vertices are unique (subsingleton), so the two agree and the vertex must be the second one.

Instance: SL(n,R) carries the discrete topology when the matrix space does. The whole argument is delegated to an auto-generated private obligation, morally that the discrete topology is inherited by a subtype/injection into a discrete space.
SL(n,R) sits inside the matrix space as a subtype, and a subspace of a discrete space is discrete; the actual argument is hidden in an auto-generated private proof obligation.

SL(n,R) sits inside the finite matrix space, which is discrete when R is, so discreteness is inherited through the subtype embedding; here the actual argument is hidden behind an auto-generated private proof term.

The claim that a set is contained in the von Neumann ordinal of its own rank; here it is discharged by simp-generated rewriting that reduces the goal to reflexivity of ≤ on ordinals, with the actual content buried in a private simp lemma.

The claim that a ZF set is contained in the von Neumann set of its rank is discharged by a simp certificate that rewrites the goal to True; the actual mathematical step (rank/vonNeumann characterization plus reflexivity of ≤) is sealed inside a generated private lemma.

Simp reduces the goal to the rank characterization of membership in the von Neumann hierarchy: a set is contained in vonNeumann of an ordinal exactly when its rank is at most that ordinal, and here the ordinal is the rank itself, so reflexivity closes it.
Unfold ENNReal.ofReal as the coercion of Real.toNNReal, cancel the coercion with coe_le_coe, and reduce to the corresponding order iff for toNNReal on the reals.
Unfolds ENNReal.ofReal as the coercion of Real.toNNReal, cancels the coercion with coe_le_coe, and reduces the goal to the known iff for toNNReal comparison under nonnegativity.

Unfold ENNReal.ofReal as the coercion of Real.toNNReal, reduce the inequality of coerced NNReals to an inequality in NNReal via coe_le_coe, then apply monotonicity of toNNReal under the nonnegativity hypothesis.
Both sides unfold to the same search over the slice, so the equality of contains-with-a-Char-pattern and contains-with-the-(· == c)-predicate holds definitionally; the proof is rfl.
Pure definitional unfolding: searching a slice for a character and searching it for the predicate (· == c) reduce to the same searcher computation, so the proof is rfl.
Both sides unfold to the same search over the slice: matching a character pattern is by definition matching the boolean predicate (· == c), so the proof is definitional unfolding closed by rfl.
Push the nonnegative-real distance to the real distance via the injective coercion, then apply dist_eq_zero, which is where the genuine MetricSpace (not merely pseudometric) hypothesis is used.
Push the nonnegative-real distance through the coercion to the reals, so that nndist x y = 0 becomes dist x y = 0, and apply the metric-space separation axiom dist_eq_zero.
Push the statement through the coercion NNReal to Real: nndist x y = 0 iff its real coercion dist x y = 0, then apply dist_eq_zero for a genuine metric space.
Construct the isometric-action instance for the additive opposite: the opposite action is the original action by the unopped element, so the extended distance is unchanged by edist_vadd_left.
Construct the IsIsometricVAdd instance: unfolding the opposite action to unop, the required edist (a +ᵥ x) (a +ᵥ y) = edist x y is exactly edist_vadd_left in the underlying space.

Build the instance by checking the isometry condition: the opposite's action unops to the underlying additive action, so the extended distance is preserved by the known left-invariance lemma edist_vadd_left.
Induct on the natural number n: the base case is exp 0 = 1, and the successor step splits exp((n+1)z) via the addition formula for exp into exp(nz) * exp z, matching pow_succ.

Induction on the natural number n: exp(0 * z) = 1 = exp(z)^0, and the successor step uses exp of a sum to peel off one factor. The inductive body is compiled into a generated auxiliary definition, so the additive property of exp never appears by name.
Induction on the natural number n: the base case is exp 0 = 1, and the step splits (n+1)z as z + nz and uses the addition formula for exp together with the successor law for powers.
The starProjection form of the norm identity is the same statement as the older orthogonalProjection form, so the proof is a single application of that lemma; no new mathematics happens here.

Pure renaming: the norm identity for the star projection is exactly the previously-proved statement about the orthogonal projection onto a submodule, so the proof is a one-step delegation to that lemma.

Pure restatement: the norm of the star/orthogonal projection applied to a vector is transported from the already-proved orthogonalProjectionOnto form; no new mathematics beyond matching the two spellings.

Congruence transfer: if two arithmetic functions agree on all nonzero naturals then their L-series summability and L-series values agree, so the HasSum statements are equivalent; assembled by simp from the summability and value congruence lemmas.

Congruence for the L-series hypothesis: since the two coefficient functions agree away from 0, the L-series and its summability agree, so having a given sum is equivalent; mechanically this is a simp call closing the iff, with the real rewriting packed into a generated private simp lemma.

Since f and g agree on all nonzero naturals, their L-series terms agree, so rewrite both the summability and the value of the L-series along the congruence lemmas; the two HasSum statements then coincide and the goal closes by simp-style reflexivity.
A continuous linear map on the reals is applied to a real Gaussian; pass to the underlying linear map and quote the variance formula for a linear map of a Gaussian.
A continuous linear map on the reals is in particular a linear map, so the variance of its image of a real Gaussian is computed by the already-proved linear-map version of the formula.
A continuous linear map is in particular a linear map, so the variance of L(X) for X real Gaussian is computed by the linear-map version of the variance formula.

Obtain the witness c with b = a + c from the ExistsAddOfLE hypothesis; then a <= a + c gives 0 <= c by left-cancellation/reflection of the order; finally package the witness, the nonnegativity and the equation as the existential-and-conjunction.
From a <= b, ExistsAddOfLE produces c with b = a + c; substituting back gives a <= a + c, from which left-cancellation of <= yields 0 <= c, and the pair (c, proof) is the witness.
From a <= b, ExistsAddOfLE supplies c with b = a + c; destruct that existential, show 0 <= c from a <= a + c using the left-reflecting order hypothesis, and repackage as an existential conjunction.
Reduce a = ⊤ to ⊤ ≤ a via eq_top_iff, then feed codisjointness the two bounds a ≤ a (reflexivity) and b ≤ a.
Reduce a = ⊤ to ⊤ ≤ a via eq_top_iff, then feed codisjointness the two bounds a ≤ a (le_rfl) and b ≤ a to conclude ⊤ ≤ a.
Reduce a = top to top <= a via eq_top_iff, then use codisjointness: top <= a sup b, and both a <= a (le_rfl) and b <= a, so top <= a.
Write Ico a b as the intersection Iio b ∩ Ici a, then use that Iio is locally closed (open) and Ici is locally closed (closed) together with closure of local closedness under intersection.
Write Ico a b as the intersection Iio b ∩ Ici a, then combine local closedness of Iio (it is open) and of Ici (it is closed) using closure of locally closed sets under intersection.

Write the half-open interval as the intersection Iio b inter Ici a, then use that locally closed sets are closed under intersection together with the two known facts that Iio and Ici are locally closed.

Case split on the option: in the none branch both sides are false, in the some branch the attached subtype element has the same underlying value, so each branch closes definitionally.

Case split on the option: for none both sides are false, for some a the attached value is the subtype element with the same underlying value, so both sides reduce to p a; each branch closes by reflexivity.
Case split on the option: for none both sides are false, for some the attached element carries the same value so the predicate agrees; each branch closes by computation.

Structural induction on the red-black node, with a three-way case split on the comparison result at each node; in each branch the ordering invariant for the rebuilt subtree is re-established from the inductive hypotheses.
Structural induction on the red-black node, with a three-way case split on the comparison result, showing the insertion function preserves the Ordered invariant in each branch.

Structural induction on the red-black node together with a three-way case split on the comparison Ordering, showing each branch of ins preserves the Ordered invariant; the actual case work sits in a generated helper.
